title: Support "partially saved" password (for tokens like yubikey)
line: For OpenVPN passwords set to "Ask for this password every time", the start of the password can now be saved; the prompt fills it in and the token types the rest.
explanation: Passwords made of a fixed part plus a one-time code from a token (Yubikey) could only be saved whole, which never works, or asked every time, so the fixed part had to be typed or pasted on every connection. With "Ask for this password every time", the OpenVPN password field now stays editable (placeholder "Optional: first part of the password, filled in every time"). Whatever is typed there is saved as an agent-owned secret that is also flagged as not saved (NetworkManager flags 3), so NetworkManager hands it to plasma-nm's secret agent to store in the keychain but never on disk. While the VPN is being activated, the agent holds that partial secret back from NetworkManager's first, non-interactive request, so NetworkManager asks again interactively and the password dialog opens with the fixed part already filled in and the cursor after it (instead of selected), ready for the token to type the rest. The connection editor now also loads agent-owned secrets that carry the not-saved flag, so the saved part shows up and can be changed or cleared there.

commits.message:
openvpn: Store the first part of a password that is asked every time

Passwords made of a fixed part and a one-time code from a token had to
be typed in full on every connection. "Ask for this password every
time" now stores what is typed in its field and fills it in when asking.

BUG: 388516

media.caption: Master: with "Ask for this password every time" the password field is disabled, nothing can be saved.
With the fix: the field stays editable and keeps the saved first part (shown revealed here).
Master: connecting asks for the whole password every time.
With the fix: the prompt opens with the saved part ("StaticPart") filled in and the cursor after it; the token's code ("ccccOTP123") is typed after it.
